key_insight: ProCARE turns real-world study automation into a constrained compilation problem, using dataset-specific evidence contracts and a typed intermediate representation to reduce LLM errors in clinical analytics workflows.
clinical_relevance: For health systems and researchers, this could make automated observational study generation more reliable by better matching analyses to local data semantics, follow-up rules, and outcome definitions.
method: Converts heterogeneous data profiles into Evidence Contracts that describe available variables, time attributes, distributions, and evidentiary limits.
Compiles study objectives into RWS-IR, a strongly typed representation for variables, time relations, analysis units, and statistical tasks.
Uses deterministic validation plus localized repair to fix errors across schema mapping, cohort construction, variable derivation, analysis, and interpretation.
evidence_signal: On 36 EHR-based benchmark tasks, ProCARE outperformed strong LLM-agent baselines in code executability, semantic consistency, and conclusion traceability, with automated violation diagnoses showing moderate-to-substantial agreement with blinded expert review.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate data profiling and well-defined local evidence contracts, so deployment may be challenging when clinical semantics are incomplete, inconsistent, or poorly documented.
paper_title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts
